title: What if the students present are 33 or 27?
description: A smiley stands for ten students and a half smiley for five. Showing thirty three and twenty seven with these symbols leaves some students that no symbol can show, and Keeko's doubt, that a half smiley can show any small number, is checked against the key.
teaching_notes: One idea: a key fixes what each symbol means, so only counts built from the key's values can be shown exactly. Watch for students who think a half symbol can stand for any small number.

source: What could be the problems faced in preparing such a pictograph, if the total number of students present in a class is 33 or 27?
video_script.why: The child sees that a symbol for ten and a half symbol for five cannot show every count, which is the limit of a pictograph.
video_script.substitution: Try to build 33 and 27 from smileys of ten and half smileys of five and see what is left over.
video_script.anchor: the smiley key of ten students and half smiley of five students
video_script.wrong_answer: a half smiley can show any small number
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko thinks the half smiley can be used for any small count such as three or seven. The key fixes it at exactly five students.
video_script.payoff_line: The smileys cannot show three or seven students exactly

final_answer.value: A symbol for 10 and a half symbol for 5 cannot show 3 or 7 students exactly
final_answer.spoken: a smiley for ten and a half smiley for five cannot show three or seven students exactly

names.Jia: uses one smiley for 10 students and a half smiley for 5

maths_rules: key: 1 smiley = 10 students, half smiley = 5 students
33 - 30 = 3 students left after 3 smileys; a half smiley shows 5, which is more than 3
27 - 20 = 7 students left after 2 smileys; 7 - 5 = 2 students left after a half smiley
only counts made of tens and fives fit exactly
video_script.design: One idea: the key fixes the size of each symbol. The key stays on the board and the two awkward counts are tried against it.

beats.on_screen: a small title card From your book; the key box: one smiley for 10 students, one half smiley for 5 students; two class cards that say 33 students present and 27 students present

marks.book: the small title card From your book appears
marks.key: the key box with a smiley and a half smiley appears
marks.ask: the two class cards appear with a question mark

narration: <bookmark mark='book'/>This is a question from your book about Jia's pictograph.
<bookmark mark='key'/>Jia uses one smiley for ten students and a half smiley for five students.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>One class has thirty three students present, and another has twenty seven. What problems come up?

beats.on_screen: the key and the two class cards stay on the board and Keeko sits at the corner of the board

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

narration: <bookmark mark='think'/>Think and tell.

beats.on_screen: 25 students drawn as 2 smileys and a half smiley; 35 students drawn as 3 smileys and a half smiley; 20 + 5 = 25 and 30 + 5 = 35 are written

marks.twenty: 2 smileys and a half smiley appear for 25 students
marks.thirty: 3 smileys and a half smiley appear for 35 students

narration: <bookmark mark='twenty'/>Look at twenty five students first. Two smileys show twenty, and a half smiley shows the five that remain.
<bookmark mark='thirty'/>For thirty five students, three smileys show thirty, and a half smiley shows five more.
<bookmark mark='fit'/>These counts are built from tens and one five, so they fit.

beats.on_screen: Given: 1 smiley = 10 students, half smiley = 5 students; one class has 33 students present, another has 27

marks.classes: the two class counts are written

narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, one smiley stands for ten students, and a half smiley stands for five.
<bookmark mark='classes'/>One class has thirty three students present, and another has twenty seven.

beats.on_screen: To find: the problems in showing 33 and 27

marks.find: the words the problems are written

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find the problems in showing these two counts.

beats.on_screen: Step 1: 33 students. 3 smileys show 3 x 10 = 30; 33 - 30 = 3 students are left

marks.left: 33 - 30 = 3 is written and 3 students are shown waiting

narration: <bookmark mark='three'/>Step one, show thirty three with whole smileys, because each one stands for ten.
<bookmark mark='ten'/>Three smileys show three times ten, which is thirty.
<bookmark mark='left'/>Thirty three take away thirty leaves three students.

beats.on_screen: Step 2: the half smiley shows 5, but only 3 students are left; 5 is more than 3

marks.half: a half smiley is placed beside the 3 waiting students

narration: <bookmark mark='half'/>Step two, try the half smiley for these three students, because it is the smallest symbol.
<bookmark mark='more'/>It shows five students, and five is more than three.

beats.on_screen: Step 3: 27 students. 2 smileys show 2 x 10 = 20; 27 - 20 = 7; a half smiley shows 5; 7 - 5 = 2 students are left

marks.rest: a half smiley takes 5 and 7 - 5 = 2 students are left over

narration: <bookmark mark='two'/>Step three, show twenty seven. Two smileys show two times ten, which is twenty.
<bookmark mark='seven'/>Twenty seven take away twenty leaves seven students.
<bookmark mark='rest'/>A half smiley takes five of them, and seven take away five leaves two students without a symbol.

beats.on_screen: Answer: a smiley for 10 and a half smiley for 5 cannot show 3 or 7 students exactly

marks.why: the words only tens and fives light up

narration: <bookmark mark='pay'/>The smileys cannot show three or seven students exactly.
<bookmark mark='why'/>Whole smileys and half smileys show only tens and fives. A symbol cannot be cut into smaller bits.

beats.on_screen: Keeko with a raised hand beside the key box
narration: <bookmark mark='hand'/>Keeko has raised a hand. Let us check the doubt and solve it.

beats.on_screen: Keeko's bubble says a half smiley can show any small number; the half smiley is labelled 5 beside a heap of 3 students and a heap of 7 students, and it matches neither; the bubble is struck through

marks.five: the half smiley is labelled 5 in the key
marks.cant: the half smiley is held beside 3 students and 7 students and matches neither; the bubble is struck through

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks a half smiley can show any small number.
<bookmark mark='five'/>Look at the key. A half smiley always means exactly five students.
<bookmark mark='cant'/>It cannot become three or seven, so it does not fit every small number.
